Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

from collections import deque, defaultdict

def clusters(I,bg):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); seen=set()
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if I[i][j]!=bg and (i,j) not in seen:
                q=deque([(i,j)]); seen.add((i,j)); cl=[]
                while q:
                    a,b=q.popleft(); cl.append((a,b))
                    for da,db in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        x,y=a+da,b+db
                        if 0<=x<H and 0<=y<W and I[x][y]==I[a][b] and (x,y) not in seen:
                            seen.add((x,y)); q.append((x,y))
                yield I[a][b],sorted(cl)

def solve(I):
    bg=I[0][0]
    bycolor=defaultdict(list)
    for v,c in clusters(I,bg): bycolor[v].extend(c)
    # candidate shifts: keep those where every cluster maps into its OWN color's output bbox; derive from color groups directly
    opt={}  # v -> list of (dr,dc) valid relative to its own bounding box, ignoring collisions
    cand=[]
    for v in sorted(bycolor):
        cells=[p for p in bycolor[v]]
        rs=[p[0] for p in cells]; cs_=[p[1] for p in cells]
        R1,R0=min(rs),max(rs); C1,C0=min(cs_),max(cs_)
        h=R1-R0+1; w=C1-C0+1
        valid=[]
        for dr in range(-R0, R1+1):
            for dc in range(-C0, C1+1):
                rr=[p[0]+dr for p in cells]; cc=[p[1]+dc for p in cells]
                if max(rr)-min(rr)+1==h and max(cc)-min(cc)+1==w:
                    valid.append((dr,dc))
        opt[v]=valid
    # choose per color shift that packs optimally; enumerate assignments jointly minimizing bbox
    ncolors=len(opt); keys=list(opt)
    best=None
    def rec(k,used,ranges,area,cellsmap):
        global best
        if k==ncolors:
            if best is None or area<best[0]: best=(area,ranges,cellsmap)
            return
        v=keys[k]
        for dr,dc in opt[v]:
            pass
        h=w=0
        rec2(v,k,ranges,area,h,w,cellsmap)
    rec2(None,0,{},0,0,{})

    def rec2(k,ranges,area,h,w,cellsmap):
        global best
        if k==ncolors:
            if best is None or area<(best[0],best[1]): best=(area,(ranges,cellsmap))
            return
        v=keys[k]
        cells=bycolor[v]
        for dr,dc in opt[v]:
            newr=[p[0]+dr for p in cells]; newc=[p[1]+dc for p in cells]
            nh,nw=max(newr)-min(newr)+1,max(newc)-min(newc)+1
            if nh+w*0<0: pass
            newarea=h*w+(nh*nw)>0 and (nh*nw+h*w)
            # tentative collision-free check requires full layout -> defer
            r2=ranges|{(v,newr,min(newr),max(newr))}
            rec3(k+1,r2,newarea+0,area,h,w,cellsmap)
    rec3(0,{},0,0,0,0,{})
    rec3=None
    def rec3(k,ranges,curarea,ah,aw,cellsmap):
        global best
        if k==ncolors:
            cand_final=(curarea,(ranges,cellsmap))
            if best is None or cand_final<best: best=cand_final
            return
        v=keys[k]
        cells=bycolor[v]
        for dr,dc in opt[v]:
            newr=[p[0]+dr for p in cells]; newc=[p[1]+dc for p in cells]
            nh,nw=max(newr)-min(newr)+1,max(newc)-min(newc)+1
            nh=nw=0
            # collision: any cell of v lands on existing? none (different color sets assumed distinct cells) - distinct colors, disjoint
            # bbox union area: sum of individual areas minus overlaps of bboxes? approximated
            pass
    # fallback: simple iterative pick: at each step pick color whose shift minimizes resulting total bbox area given current layout, checking no collision among cells
    occ={}; res={}
    picked=[]
    remaining=[v for v in keys]
    while remaining:
        v=remaining.pop()
        cells=bycolor[v]
        best_v=None
        for dr,dc in opt[v]:
            nr=[p[0]+dr for p in cells]; nc=[p[1]+dc for p in cells]
            h_=max(nr)-min(nr)+1; w_=max(nc)-min(nc)+1
            r0_,c0_=min(nr),min(nc)
            # check collision with occ
            ok=all(not any((r0_+a, c0_+b)==q for q in occ) for a,b in [(r0_+x,c0_+y) for x,y in zip(nr,nc)])
            if not ok: continue
            score=(max(nr)-min(nr)+1)*(max(nc)-min(nc)+1)
            if best_v is None or score<best_v[0]:
                best_v=(score,(dr,dc),(min(nr),min(nc)))
        if best_v is None: break
        _,(dr,dc),(r0_,c0_)=best_v
        for a,b in cells:
            occ[(a+dr,b+dc)]=v
        res[v]=(dr,dc)
    # build output grid: bbox of occ, fill bg elsewhere
    rs=[p[0] for p in occ]; cs_=[p[1] for p in occ]
    r0,c0=min(rs),min(cs_)
    out=[[bg]*(max(cs_)-c0+1) for _ in range(r0,max(rs)+1)]
    for (r_,c_),v in occ.items(): out[r_-r0][c_-c0]=v
    # crop to tight bbox of nonzero
    nz=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(out) for c,x in enumerate(row) if x!=bg]
    r1,c1=max(r for r,_ in nz),max(c for _,c in nz)
    return [[out[r][c] for c in range(c0,c1+1)] for r in range(r0,r1+1)], keys

# Verify the PACKING hypothesis: drop the rarest color's cells entirely; recolor remaining canvas cells of that color to bg; then move every kept object up-left maximally
# without overlap, scanning TLs in increasing order. Out = bbox of placed cells.
def f(gi):
    H,W=len(gi),len(gi[0]); bgi=gi[0][0]
    cs=comps(gi,bgi)
    cnt=Counter(v for v,_ in cs)
    mv=min(cnt,key=lambda v:(cnt[v], tuple(sorted(min(p) for p in [])) ))
    # pick most frequent among single-comp colors when tie -> use lexicographic tiebreak
    cand=[v for v,c in cnt.items()]
    cmin=min(cnt.values())
    ties=[v for v in cand if cnt[v]==cmin]
    mv=min(ties)  # smallest value color with min count
    occ=set()
    objs=[]
    for v,c in cs:
        if v==mv: continue
        objs.append((v,c))
    objs.sort(key=lambda vc:(min(p[0] for p in vc[1]),min(p[1] for p in vc[1])))
    out=[[mv]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for v,c in objs:
        r0=min(p[0] for p in c); c0=min(p[1] for p in c)
        dr=-r0; dc=-c0
        while True:
            okp=True
            for (r,j) in c:
                nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
                if nr<0 or nc<0 or (nr,nc) in occ: okp=False;break
            if okp: break
            dr-=1; dc-=1
        for (r,j) in c: out[r+dr][j+dc]=v
        for (r,j) in c: occ.add((r+dr,j+dc))
    # crop to occupied bbox
    rs=[p[0] for p in occ]; cs_=[p[1] for p in occ]
    return [row[min(cs_) : max(cs_)+1] for row in out[max(rs):max(rs)+1]]
for n in range(1,9):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    r=f(gi)
    print(n, r==go, len(r),'x',len(r[0]),'vs',len(go),'x',len(go[0]))

import numpy as np
# Hypothesis: take input bounding box of all non-bg cells, crop it (remove bg-only rows/cols inside?). Test on pair 4 & others.
def bboxcrop(g):
    g=np.array(g); bg=g[0,0]
    H,W=g.shape
    rows=[r for r in range(H) if any(g[r,c]!=bg for c in range(W))]
    cols=[c for c in range(W) if any(g[r,c]!=bg for r in range(H))]
    return g[np.ix_(rows,cols)]
for p in [3,4,5,6,7,8]:

def load_file(path):
    t=open(path,errors='ignore').read().replace('\\n','\n')
    G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
